title: First-level Fourier coefficients and query cost
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $0<p<1$, and let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ independent signs, with real-valued outputs, that computes a function $f$. Under the product distribution in which each sign is $-1$ with probability $p$, the square of the sum of the biased Fourier coefficients of $f$ indexed by the singleton coordinate sets is at most the second moment of $f$ times the expected number of queries made by $T$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite coordinate set of size n
A real-valued decision tree on sign inputs
A function f on sign inputs
